baseline:
B
A sine wave is a continuous, periodic function that is spread out over all time. In contrast, a single square pulse is a non-periodic event that is localized, existing only for a finite duration.

B
The Fourier Transform is a mathematical operation that converts a signal from its time-domain representation (how its amplitude changes over time) to its frequency-domain representation (which frequencies make up the signal).

B
This is a direct consequence of the Uncertainty Principle for Fourier transforms, which states that a function cannot be simultaneously narrow in both the time and frequency domains. A larger spread (variance) in time corresponds to a smaller, more concentrated spread (variance) in frequency, and vice versa.

D
The uncertainty principle states that a signal cannot be precisely localized in both time and frequency simultaneously. As a signal becomes shorter and more localized in time (like a cheetah's short chirp), its frequency content becomes less certain and spreads out over a wider range.

B
This is a statement of the time-frequency uncertainty principle. A signal that is very short and sharply defined in time (like a clap) is necessarily composed of a wide range of frequencies. Conversely, a signal with a very narrow, pure frequency (like a sustained note from a tuning fork) must extend over a longer period of time. It is a fundamental physical and mathematical trade-off, not a technological limitation.
